system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

Individual CBS messages will be assigned their own geographical coverage areas by mutual agreement between the information provider and the PLMN or SNPN operator. CBS messages may originate from a number of Cell Broadcast Entities (CBEs), which are connected to the Cell Broadcast Centre. A CBS page comprises of 82 octets, which, using the default character set, equates to 93 characters. Other Data Coding Schemes may also be used, as described in 3GPP TS 23.038 [3]. Up to 15 of these pages may be concatenated to form a CBS messagee. Each page of such CBS message will have the same message identifier (indicating the source of the message), and the same serial number. data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present, and both are well under the 15-page limit (en 3 pages GSM-7, ar 6 pages UCS-2). Page length is already covered by recorded gap G6, so I do not object to it, including TS040's 1-page guidance. The problem is that neither language gives any protective action, on the first page or anywhere else. The text describes the hazard (blowing dust and sand, low visibility), its timing and its source, but never tells people what to do. The drafter can fix this.

objections.issue: No protective action appears in either language, so the first page carries the hazard but not the action. People receive a description of the dust storm with no instruction on what to do.
objections.fix: Add a short protective action in both English and Arabic, placed right after the hazard so it falls on the first page. For example, EN: 'Drive with care, keep your distance and use low-beam headlights; people with asthma or breathing problems should stay indoors.' Give AR an equivalent near the start, e.g. 'قودوا بحذر واتركوا مسافة كافية واستخدموا الأضواء المنخفضة؛ ويُنصح مرضى الربو والجهاز التنفسي بالبقاء في الداخل.' Keep the hazard and action together at the start of each text, and recheck that each language stays within 15 pages.
